brief: Goldman's TMT sales desk flags AI voice agents (Meta's Muse, rival Instinct) that can call businesses to negotiate phone and cable bills as a new risk to telcos: US telco shares fell (TMUS -5.5%, AT&T -2%, VZ -3%) on chatter that such agents can wait on hold, switch users to cheaper plans, remove add-ons and claim credits at scale, pressuring ARPU and retention economics. The desk extends this risk to any industry with recurring bills, negotiable pricing and high switching friction (cable, insurance, utilities, banks, subscriptions, travel). Separately, Korean media reports critical semicap component lead times have worsened sharply (deposition parts from about 4 to 10 months, packaging parts about 50% longer, laser equipment up to 40 months from Japan) because makers are reluctant to use Chinese suppliers amid trade tensions, reinforcing tight supply even as it risks delaying equipment makers' own deliveries. GS raises its 2027 hyperscaler gross debt issuance forecast to $420bn, over 60% above its $250bn 2026 estimate. On Adyen, the desk calls the Stripe Link disintermediation bear case overstated given Adyen's multi-standard agentic-payments positioning. TEF is reportedly cooling on a Vodafone Spain deal after Zegona's stock jumped on takeout hopes, with a wide valuation gap the sticking point, as TEF appears more focused on German consolidation instead.
